The heating system turns on a few hours later in the upgraded scenario, indicating that wall insulation and advanced air sealing keep the home warmer during the night and into early morning, so the heat does not need to run until later in the morning. The heating peak is also significantly reduced. Both results are in line with expectations. Finally, the Arizona model’s upgraded cooling energy profile is lower than the profile for all hours on July 1. The curve is smaller and has a lower peak as well. These results are consistent with the other two example buildings and the expected outcomes. 4.1.2 Example Annual Individual Building Results In general, the three individual buildings each show savings in total annual site energy. Although the set of measures modeled here differ from those in other studies, the amounts are generally consistent with the magnitude of savings from typical envelope upgrades (Baechler, et al. 2021) (Polly, et al. 2011) (ENERGY STAR n.d.). In all three building models, both cooling and heating energy consumption show annual savings. Cooling and heating peak loads also show reductions ranging from slight to considerable.
